finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication or org-ownership check, so any unauthenticated network client can list user ids and names for any org by passing the org query parameter.
finding.sink: db.js:9 req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1 (returns rows via db.js:10 res.json)

trace.note: app.listen(3002) with no host argument, so the server binds to all interfaces by default
/users route handler registered with no auth middleware or guard
org taken directly from req.query.org and used as the filter for the user query
all matching id and name rows returned as JSON to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware (app.use) or per-route guard exists in db.js. The SQL is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. The org filter is caller-supplied and does not restrict who may read. req.pg is not set in this file, so the connection wiring and any auth layer outside this repo were not visible and could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js has no app.use middleware and no per-route guard on /users (db.js:8-11). The SQL is parameterized (db.js:9, $1), so injection is not a factor, and the org filter is caller-supplied. The only other file in the directory is db.js, so req.pg (db.js:9) is not set here and no upstream auth layer is visible.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: req.query.org is read at db.js:9 and rows are returned at db.js:10 with no guard in db.js:8-11, and app.listen(3002) at db.js:23 has no host argument so it listens on all interfaces. The finding holds for this repo, with the caveat that an auth layer injected via req.pg or a fronting proxy outside this repo could not be checked.
